summary: HTTP/3 (QUIC) artifact downloads stall due to MSS clamping by customer WAN optimizer on private deployment
description:
Issue summary: Customers report large model artifact downloads (several MBs) initiated from private deployment nodes frequently hang during the HTTP/3 (QUIC) handshake or immediately after transfer start. Smaller artifacts succeed; downloads over ~1200-1400 bytes commonly stall and eventually time out.

Impact: Model pulls for new serving nodes and periodic artifact refreshes fail, causing increased cold-start times and degraded scaling for NimbleAnalytics' private deployment. Customer reports multiple failed rollouts and a production impact on inference availability.

Environment: Private deployment connected to Redwood via VPCE and a customer-managed WAN optimizer appliance for egress. Client: node-exporter on private serving nodes using our artifact fetcher (default HTTP/3 where available). Region: us-west-2 (customer-controlled egress).

Steps to reproduce:
1) Trigger model rollout on private serving pool (pull model artifact ~10MB).
2) Observe artifact fetch attempt in agent logs; client negotiates HTTP/3 with Redwood S3-presigned endpoint.
3) Transfer stalls shortly after start; repeated retries eventually fall back to HTTP/1.1 or time out depending on retry window.

Observed logs/traces:
- Agent logs: "download: http3_stream stalled after 0x1a0 bytes, retrying"
- h3 / quicserver logs: repeated PTOs (probe timeouts) and early connection closure with ERROR_TRANSPORT(0x1)
- tcpdump from customer edge (captured): multiple UDP Initial packets with QUIC token, followed by ICMP "Fragmentation needed" not seen in path; customer-managed WAN optimizer shows MSS rewrite to 1200 bytes and strips ICMP type 3 messages.
- VPC Flow Logs: no obvious packet loss on underlying ENIs; retransmits seen at optimizer interface.

Initial hypothesis: Customer WAN optimizer or edge middlebox is clamping MSS / rewriting TCP/UDP segmentation parameters and also suppressing ICMP PMTU messages. QUIC relies on PMTU discovery and large initial UDP frames — when PMTU discovery is blocked and MSS/MSS-clamping reduces allowable payloads but the optimizer does not properly re-segment or generate CLAMP-correct behavior for UDP/QUIC, QUIC initial packets are dropped or cause PTOs leading to stalls. HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 (TCP) fallback works more often because TCP path can negotiate smaller MSS or be retransmitted in a way the appliance handles.

Requested from customer: packet capture (pcap) at WAN optimizer ingress/egress with timestamps, configuration snippet showing MSS/MTU rewrite rules, and confirmation on whether ICMP Type 3 (Fragmentation Needed) is blocked or dropped.
comments: 2026-03-09 09:12 - Customer (NimbleAnalytics): We're seeing model downloads hang during rollouts. Small models OK, larger ones time out. This started after we enabled our new WAN optimizer appliance last week.

2026-03-09 10:03 - Support (Aisha Patel): Thanks — can you share a pcap from the edge and a config sample for the optimizer? Also confirm whether you observe any ICMP 'fragmentation needed' messages being dropped.

2026-03-09 11:47 - Customer: Attached pcap and config excerpt. We found logs on the optimizer indicating 'MSS clamping to 1200' for outgoing connections. We do not intentionally drop ICMP but the appliance has an option to suppress ICMP generation.

2026-03-09 15:30 - SRE (Miguel Ramirez): Reviewing pcap: QUIC Initial packets sent with ~1350-1400B UDP payloads; appliance rewrites/forwards UDP but drops/doesn't forward subsequent large packets. No ICMP Type 3 seen leaving optimizer toward Redwood. Hypothesis: MSS/MTU clamp + ICMP suppression causing PMTU blackhole for QUIC.

2026-03-09 17:04 - Support (Aisha): As a near-term workaround, we can force artifact fetches to use HTTP/1.1 for your private pool (will increase latency). Would you like us to enable HTTP/1.1 fallback on your deployment while you work with the optimizer vendor?
2026-03-09 18:20 - Customer: Please enable HTTP/1.1 fallback for the rollout window. We'll engage our network team and vendor to test disabling MSS clamping / allowing ICMP.
investigation:
- Packet-level findings: Initial QUIC Initial packets from our edge to client show client sends ACKs for small amounts then stalls. The optimizer rewrites MSS to 1200 and appears to fragment or drop large UDP datagrams. No ICMP Fragmentation Needed messages are forwarded from inside customer network to Redwood; vendor config shows 'suppress-pmtu-icmp true'.
- Reproduction on support side: In a lab with a simulated optimizer set to clamp MTU to 1200 and suppress ICMP, HTTP/3 downloads fail to complete for large payloads while HTTP/1.1 completes after retransmit.
- Instrumentation: Added additional retry telemetry in artifact fetcher to record protocol used and time to fallback; early telemetry shows fallback occurs after multiple PTOs (~6s).
- Short-term mitigation validated: Forcing HTTP/1.1 path for artifact fetch increases success rate to ~99% in customer topology.
resolution:
- Workaround applied: Support enabled HTTP/1.1-first artifact fetch policy for NimbleAnalytics' private serving pool to avoid QUIC path; this reduces stalls during rollouts (applied 2026-03-09 20:15).
- Permanent fix recommended for customer: disable MSS clamping for traffic toward Redwood endpoints and allow ICMP Type 3 (Fragmentation Needed) to pass, or configure optimizer to properly re-segment UDP/QUIC flows.
- Product follow-up actions: 1) Add a config knob to force artifact fetcher to use TCP-only for private deployments as an operator-level toggle (tracked in GH PR referenced). 2) Add detection telemetry that flags likely PMTU/ICMP suppression when QUIC PTOs spike during artifact downloads.
- Customer validation: NimbleAnalytics network team scheduled vendor change for 2026-03-11 to allow ICMP and disable MSS clamp; tentative follow-up planned after vendor test.
- Status: Workaround in place; awaiting customer network changes to restore HTTP/3 native path.
